subject: physics
question_text: The speeds of four gas molecules (in km/s) are 1, 2, 3 and 4. Find the rms speed of the molecules.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Short Answer Question 6 (printed p.140). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: v_rms = √((1²+2²+3²+4²)/4) = √(30/4) = √7.5 = 2.74 km/s, and the ordinary average speed (1+2+3+4)/4 = 2.5 km/s is a different, smaller number, matching the brief's independently checked arithmetic.

steps.label: Formula
lines: The rms speed is the square root of the
mean of the squares of the speeds:
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the definition before touching the numbers.
steps.why: The ordinary mean of the speeds can hide how spread out they are, so kinetic theory always works with the mean of the squares first.
common_mistakes: Writing the formula as the square of the mean instead of the mean of the squares.
steps.memory_tip: Square first, then average, then take the root — square, mean, root.

steps.label: Sum of the squares
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Square each speed separately, then add.
steps.why: Each speed is squared on its own before the four squares are added — squaring is not linear, so this step cannot be skipped.
common_mistakes: Adding the speeds first and squaring the total: (1+2+3+4)² is not the same as 1²+2²+3²+4².
steps.memory_tip: 1, 4, 9, 16 — the first four square numbers, added to 30.

steps.label: Mean of the squares
lines: This mean, 7.5, is found BEFORE the
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Divide by N = 4 while the values are still squared.
steps.why: The mean must be taken of the squared values, not of the original speeds — this is the step most answers skip straight past.
common_mistakes: Dividing 30 by 4 and calling it the rms speed directly, without taking the square root that follows.
steps.memory_tip: Thirty over four is seven point five — the mean SQUARED speed, not the answer yet.

steps.label: rms speed
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Take the square root, then compare with the ordinary average.
steps.why: The square root of the mean square is always at least as large as the ordinary mean, because squaring gives extra weight to the larger speeds — that is why 2.74 km/s is larger than the plain average of 2.5 km/s.
common_mistakes: Reporting the ordinary average speed, 2.5 km/s, as the rms speed.
Rounding √7.5 to 2.7 without carrying enough figures.
steps.memory_tip: rms is always a little bigger than the plain average: 2.74 against 2.5.

insider_note: This question is testing whether the student knows rms speed is not the ordinary average. Show 7.5 as the mean of the squares, then contrast 2.74 km/s with the plain average, 2.5 km/s.
